gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-days-one: Tube-like letters, no swelling anywhere: Tilt Neon keeps its stroke constant from end to end. Days One brings an x-height that fills the line and spacing like rungs on a rope ladder.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-farro: Farro keeps its ascenders short and its strokes entirely without contrast, which leaves plenty of room for Tilt Neon to be loud. Tilt Neon grabs attention; Farro simply carries the words.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-hammersmith-one: Tubes above, cord below: Tilt Neon has a constant-width stroke, while Hammersmith One rounds its strokes like cut lengths of cord. Page after page, Hammersmith One would stay low and soft.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-inder: A constant stroke with no calligraphic thinning defines Tilt Neon, with its large x-height and short ascenders. Inder would read smoothly over a full page, since its capitals and lowercase differ so little in height.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-jaldi: Loud, constant-stroke tubes: Tilt Neon gives its y a tail matching its arm in thickness. Jaldi does the quieter job, brushed letters packed close with a tall x-height and a gaping c.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-kdam-thmor-pro: Bowls that fill the line give the body a contemporary feel beneath Tilt Neon, whose stroke never thins at the shoulders. Kdam Thmor Pro would keep a dense, modern rhythm going page after page.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-martian-mono: Tube-like and loud, Tilt Neon sits over a monospace body. Martian Mono sets fixed-width, code-style letters well apart, with generous openings in every curve, and that structure is the real hook.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-menbere: Menbere stacks its lowercase tall like rolled cord, leaving a quiet, clean texture under the heading. Tilt Neon bends thin steel rod into every letter, so the two feel distinctly different.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-mitr: A stroke that never changes weight gives Tilt Neon a skimming ease, with a large x-height and short ascenders. Mitr would read in a compact, friendly way, since its caps sit very close to the x-height.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-mukta-mahee: Tilt Neon draws straight-edged, constant strokes in a bold, commanding voice. Mukta Mahee is chunkier and taller in the lowercase, so pages of text would still feel approachable and clean.
